learning: If slalom progress rises above 0.33 and max_error falls toward 0.06 m with oval and s-bend completion holding, reversal reaction was the lever and kp can go a little higher. If s-bend completion drops or oscillation rises sharply, return kp to 2.4. If progress stays flat near 0.32, the controller is saturated and the next test is wheel_track of about 0.10 m.
notes: Geometry is the iteration-8 geometry held exactly, as the Builder proposed. The controller is the iteration-8 controller with kp raised from 2.4 to 2.8, so kp is the only controller variable.
rationale:
Iteration 8 is the best race so far (673.8). Oval and s-bend both complete 20 of 20. The slalom still fails 0 of 20, with progress 0.32, max_error 0.0635 m and 1.05 line-loss events per run. The Builder's iteration-9 geometry is the same as iteration 8, so the geometry is held and only the controller changes.

The integral term is near saturation. Raising ki from 0.4 to 0.7 added only about 0.26 to the score, and slalom progress moved from about 0.319 to 0.320. Line losses are about 1 per run, well below the 2-per-run widening trigger, so sensing is not the limit. Look-ahead was saturated at y = 0.07 m in iteration 5. The remaining slalom failure looks like reaction on the reversal.

The one controller change I make is kp from 2.4 to 2.8, to add correction per unit of signal on the reversal. kd stays at 0.8 to damp the extra gain, since oval oscillation is 0.19 and s-bend is 0.29, and iteration 1 showed that gain without damping raised oscillation. ki stays at 0.7, base_speed 1.3 and last_direction line loss are unchanged. I expect slalom max_error to fall toward 0.06 m with oval and s-bend completion holding. This is a hypothesis, not a measured result. The main risk is oscillation on the s-bend, which would show as lower completion.
